answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each identity write its own record with a quill of graded work: a newcomer posts a small bond that unlocks only after peer-graded contributions spread across several epochs, not a fable finished in a day. A fake army would need genuine graded work behind every identity, and since established peers check originality, that work cannot be bought in bulk or run in parallel; each fake pays the full slow price, while honest histories pool into a shared lagoon of trust that deepens with every verified contribution.
